sections.label: Cyber Security Agency formed
sections.summary: The Cyber Security Agency of Singapore was formed in 2015 as the central agency overseeing and coordinating Singapore's cybersecurity strategy.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: The Cyber Security Agency of Singapore (CSA) was formed in 2015 as the central agency to oversee and coordinate Singapore's cybersecurity strategy.

sections.label: MINDEF and MHA cyber bodies
sections.summary: MINDEF will set up the Defence Cyber Organisation, and MHA launched the National Cybercrime Action Plan last year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: The Ministry of Defence (MINDEF) will be setting up the Defence Cyber Organisation (DCO), which will take charge of developing the military's cyber defence capabilities.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: The Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) launched the National Cybercrime Action Plan (NCAP) last year, which sets out the Government's key priorities and strategies to combat cybercrime.

sections.label: Police CMCA cases 2016
sections.summary: In 2016, the Police investigated 691 cases under CMCA.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: In 2016, the Police investigated 691 cases under CMCA.

sections.label: Bill strengthens Police cybercrime enforcement
sections.summary: The Bill seeks to strengthen the operational effectiveness of the Police in dealing with cybercrime.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: With our high Internet penetration rate, it is even more important that we safeguard ourselves against cybercrime and enable ourselves to take firm enforcement action against criminals who make use of the anonymity and borderless nature of the Internet to commit cybercrimes.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: This Bill, therefore, seeks to strengthen the operational effectiveness of the Police in dealing with cybercrime.

sections.label: New section 8A personal information offence
sections.summary: The new section 8A closes the gap by making it an offence to obtain or deal in such personal information.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: The new section 8A, therefore, closes the gap by making it an offence to obtain or deal in such personal information.

sections.label: Clause 4 Singapore jurisdiction computer offences
sections.summary: Clause 4 amends section 11 to give Singapore jurisdiction over computer offences causing or risking serious harm in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Clause 4 amends section 11 to give Singapore jurisdiction over computer offences, where the act causes or creates a significant risk of serious harm in Singapore.

sections.label: Extraterritorial offences and serious harm
sections.summary: The amendment gives extraterritorial effect to offences causing serious harm in Singapore, defined to include illness, injury, death, and disruption of essential services and government duties.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: The amendment will give extraterritorial effect to these offences, if the act resulted in serious harm or created a significant risk of such harm in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: The Police will collaborate with their foreign counterparts to provide and share evidence of such cases, with a view to extraditing these offenders to Singapore where possible and prosecuting them before Singapore Courts.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: As extending the jurisdiction of the Act extraterritorially is not something that we do lightly, we have scoped the definition of the phrase "serious harm in Singapore" carefully, so as to ensure that Police resources will only be used to investigate cases with significant impact in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: The phrase "serious harm in Singapore" has been defined to include, among other things: illness, injury or death of individuals in Singapore; disruption of essential services in Singapore; and disruption of the carrying out of governmental duties and functions.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: These would include acts, such as unauthorised access of bank account details belonging to customers of a bank in Singapore, and publication of the medical records of patients of a local hospital.

sections.label: Stolen servicemen personal data
sections.summary: The incident led to personal data, including NRIC and telephone numbers, of around 850 servicemen and employees being stolen.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The incident led to personal data, including NRIC numbers and telephone numbers, of around 850 servicemen and employees being stolen.

sections.label: Offence of obtaining leaked personal information
sections.summary: New section 8A makes it an offence to obtain, retain, supply or make available personal information known or believed to be obtained through unauthorised access.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: First, the new section 8A of the Bill makes it an offence for a person to obtain, retain, supply or make available personal information that he or she knew or had reason to believe that it was obtained through unauthorised access to a programme or computer system.

sections.label: Grey market for customer data
sections.summary: A 2014 Tech In Asia article reported a Singapore grey market selling data, with customer data bought for about 1.2 Singapore cents apiece.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: According to a Tech In Asia article in 2014, it was reported, worryingly in my respectful view, that there exists a grey market in Singapore for sale of data.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: It further states that tons of customer data can be bought for a dirt cheap price of about 1.2 Singapore cents apiece.

sections.label: UK data sale offence
sections.summary: In the UK, the Data Protection Act makes it an offence to sell personal data knowingly or recklessly obtained without the data controller's consent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In contrast, the sale of personal data by a person who knowingly or recklessly obtained such data without the consent of the data controller has been made an offence in the UK through their Data Protection Act.

sections.label: Serious harm definition and extradition
sections.summary: The definition of serious harm does not appear to cover disruptions to commercial businesses, and the member asks the Government to consider expanding it and updating extradition offences.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The definition of "serious harm in Singapore" in the section does not appear to include situations where unauthorised access to computer material causes significant disruptions to commercial businesses in Singapore which may not be regarded as "essential services" under section 15A(12) of the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: For example, if there were to be a simultaneous DDoS attack on all Singapore e-commerce sites over a sustained period of time, this may have a severe impact on the businesses of these Singapore companies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Perhaps, we may consider expanding the definition of "serious harm" to include damage to the economy of Singapore, similar to what the UK has provided for in its Computer Misuse Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Would the Government please consider updating the list of offences for which extradition may be made possible under the Extradition Act?

sections.label: MINDEF I-net breach
sections.summary: MINDEF's I-net system was breached, and personal details of 850 National Servicemen and staff were stolen in a targeted cyberattack.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Recently, MINDEF's I-net system was breached and the personal details of 850 National Servicemen and staff at MINDEF were stolen in what MINDEF has described as a "targeted and carefully planned" cyberattack.

sections.label: Computer Misuse Amendment Bill changes
sections.summary: The Computer Misuse and Cybersecurity (Amendment) Bill introduces four main changes, including a new offence for obtaining, retaining or supplying personal information from cybercrime.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The Computer Misuse and Cybersecurity (Amendment) Bill introduces four main changes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: One, creating a new offence to obtain, retain or supply personal information obtained through an earlier act of cybercrime.

sections.label: Clause 3 proof particulars
sections.summary: Clause 3 provides a new section 8A(6) removing the need for prosecution to prove particulars of contravention, such as who and when.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Clause 3 provides for a new section 8A(6), and I quote: "For the purpose of proving under subsection (1) that a person knows or has reason to believe that any personal information was obtained by an act done in contravention of sections 3, 4, 5 or 6, it is not necessary for the prosecution to prove the particulars of contravention, such as who carried out the contravention and when it took place." This section is doing away with the need for the prosecution to prove the particulars of contravention, such as who carried out the contravention and when it took place.

sections.label: NUS data science training
sections.summary: The National University of Singapore will provide data science training for 10,000 public servants to apply technology and use data and digital tools more effectively.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The National University of Singapore will also provide data science training for 10,000 public servants, helping them to apply technology with ease and use data and digital tools more effectively.

sections.label: National Trade Platform 2018
sections.summary: The National Trade Platform, operational in 2018, would let enterprises and the Government exchange information, lower costs and simplify trade processes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For example, the National Trade Platform (NTP), which is being set up and will be operational in 2018, would allow enterprises and the Government to exchange information, help enterprises to lower their costs and simplify trade processes.

sections.label: NTP cyber protection and offences
sections.summary: NTP is important trade infrastructure that should be in cyber protection scope, and businesses should heed the amended Bill's section 8B offences.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: NTP is one of Singapore's most important trade infrastructures in the cyberworld and ought to be in the scope of cyber protection.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I would also urge businesses to pay heed to the newly amended Bill, especially in the newly inserted section 8B on criminal offences: anyone who obtains, retains, sells, creates, supplies or uses whichever method to commit computer-related offences, or deliberately allows these products to be used, would be committing an offence.

sections.label: Protection for non-essential service enterprises
sections.summary: Businesses hope the Government will expand protection to non-essential service companies so they are not cyberattack targets.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: However, when cyberattacks cause a certain degree of harm to "enterprises engaged in non-essential services", it would also involve public interests and deserve legal protection.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Hence, businesses hope that the Government can expand the protection scope and protect companies in the "non-essential service" areas as well, so that they do not become the target or victim of cyberattacks or transboundary crimes.

sections.label: Extraterritorial effect for computer offences
sections.summary: Clause 4 amends section 11 to give the statute extraterritorial effect for overseas offenders or overseas-targeted attacks.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In particular, I commend clause 4, Madam, that amends section 11 to give the statute extraterritorial effect to ensure that even if computer misuse or a cyberattack is committed by a person who is overseas at the time of the misuse or attack, or targeted at an overseas computer, the law will not be confounded by technicalities.

sections.label: Further cybersecurity legislation questions
sections.summary: The Member asks whether further cybersecurity legislation is planned, including audits, incident reporting and mandated exercises.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: First, does the Ministry intend to propose perhaps further cybersecurity legislation beyond the current amendment in the near future that will aim to give the authorities powers to audit the business sectors and organisations to ensure that they have cyber defence systems in place?

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Two, will the new laws impose perhaps extensive incident reporting, audits, risk assessments and facilitate the sharing of cybersecurity information, and perhaps even mandate the participation of critical information infrastructure operators in cybersecurity exercises?

sections.label: Secure Mobile Centre and prevention efforts
sections.summary: The Member asks if the Ministry will enhance detection and prevention efforts alongside centres like the Secure Mobile Centre.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This centre aims to create a novel ICT solution to secure different layers of mobile computing systems and to assess the scalability and usability of such new technologies and solutions to conduct experiments in real-world settings, so as to guard against such attacks in the future.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Thus, Madam, my question to the Ministry would be, apart from prosecution and investigation leading to prosecution, will the Ministry be enhancing its efforts aimed at detection and prevention, in tandem with centres, such as the Secure Mobile Centre?

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This Bill aims to address the increasing scale and transnational nature of cybercrime, as well as the evolving tactics of cybercriminals' punishable offences.

sections.label: MINDEF servicemen personal data stolen
sections.summary: Personal data of 850 Singaporean National Servicemen were stolen after a targeted cyberattack on MINDEF's Internet system.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Closer to home, we have heard personal data of 850 Singaporean National Servicemen were stolen after a targeted cyberattack on MINDEF's Internet system.

sections.label: Extraterritorial application for computer offences
sections.summary: Clause 4 seeks to give extraterritorial application to computer offences.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: First, clause 4 seeks to give extraterritorial application to computer offences.

sections.label: Cybersecurity Professional Scheme launch
sections.summary: The Minister for Communications and Information announced a Cybersecurity Professional Scheme to double public sector cybersecurity professionals over the next few years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Last month, the Minister for Communications and Information announced the launch of a Cybersecurity Professional Scheme to double the existing pool of cybersecurity professionals in the public sector over the next few years.

sections.label: Crime rate and cybercrimes
sections.summary: Overall crime rate decreased slightly last year but online crimes are rising, making it imperative to strengthen cybersecurity laws to protect citizens.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Our overall crime rate decreased slightly last year but online crimes are on the rise.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: The fast-evolving nature of cybercrimes and our increasingly heavy digital reliance makes it imperative that we strengthen our cybersecurity laws to protect our citizens from harm.

sections.label: Extraterritorial CMCA offences
sections.summary: The speaker supports including extraterritorial application of CMCA offences that cause serious harm to Singapore, as cybercrimes are often transboundary.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: As cybercrimes are often transboundary in nature, I support the move to include an extraterritorial application of CMCA offences which cause serious harm to Singapore.

sections.label: Cybersecurity for digital economy
sections.summary: Establishing and evolving Singapore's cybersecurity blanket is critical to support its growth in the digital economy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Establishing and evolving our cybersecurity blanket is critical to support Singapore's growth in the digital economy.

sections.label: Cyberattacks in Ukraine, UK, Germany
sections.summary: Cyberattacks caused a Ukraine power blackout in December 2016, a UK agency fended off 188 serious attacks, and Germany's military system was attacked 284,000 times.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: In Ukraine, cyberattacks caused a power blackout in Ukraine in December 2016.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: In the UK, a newly set up cyber protection agency fended off 188 serious attacks in the first three months of 2017.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: In Germany, its military system was attacked 284,000 times in the first nine weeks of 2017 alone.

sections.label: Training civil servants in data science
sections.summary: NUS and GovTech have committed to train 10,000 civil servants in data science over the next five years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: In this respect, I am glad that the National University of Singapore (NUS) and the Government Technology Agency of Singapore (GovTech) have committed to train 10,000 civil servants in data science in the next five years.

sections.label: Overseas computer offences criminalised
sections.summary: The amendment criminalises offences committed in foreign jurisdictions using overseas computers, closing a loophole in the current Act.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The amendment to criminalise offences under the Bill if they are committed in foreign jurisdictions using computers overseas is overdue and closes a loophole in the current Act.

sections.label: Section 8A(6) prosecution proof
sections.summary: New section 8A(6) removes the need for prosecution to prove a contravention of those sections, requiring only knowledge or reason to believe.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The new section 8A(6) removes the need for the prosecution to prove that any of those sections of the Act was contravened in order to prove that an offence was committed under section 8A(1).

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The prosecution is only required to prove that the perpetrator knows or has reason to believe that the relevant sections were contravened.

sections.label: Clarification on safe conviction
sections.summary: The question asks the Minister to clarify why a safe conviction could not be achieved without proving a relevant section was contravened.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Further, can the Minister clarify why a safe conviction could not be achieved when the prosecution does not need to prove that a relevant section was contravened when section 8A(1) is premised on the contravention of these sections?

sections.label: Hacked client data examples
sections.summary: Statements of 647 Standard Chartered private banking clients were found on James Raj's laptop, and James Sim was charged for cracking SingPass passwords.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: The statements of 647 private banking clients of Standard Chartered Bank, which had been stored on the hacked Fuji Xerox's server, were found on James Raj's laptop.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: The second example, just last year, a former administrative assistant James Sim, he was charged for cracking the passwords of about 300 SingPass account holders in 2011 and selling the account holders' personal details to a China-based syndicate involved in sham Singapore visa applications.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: The syndicate successfully applied for 23 visas, with 20 Chinese nationals entering Singapore using these visas.

sections.label: Definition of personal information
sections.summary: Personal information in section 8A is defined in the Bill as information about an individual used to identify them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Mr Desmond Choo asked what "personal information" in section 8A would cover. "Personal information" is defined in the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: It includes information about an individual, whether true or not, which is commonly used alone or in combination with other information to identify an individual.

sections.label: Prosecuting hacked data dealers
sections.summary: The law needs to let prosecution pursue those dealing in hacked personal information without proving particulars of the actual hacking offence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: The law, therefore, needs to allow the prosecution to go after the criminal who has committed the offence of dealing in the hacked personal information, without having to also prove the particulars of the actual hacking offence, which may be impossible to fully investigate.

sections.label: Criminalising sale of hacked data
sections.summary: Criminalising the sale of personal information obtained through unauthorised means is beyond the current Bill's scope.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: As for Mr Murali Pillai's question on whether we should criminalise the sale of personal information obtained through unauthorised means, regardless of whether the information is hacked, this is beyond the scope of the current Bill.

sections.label: SME Digital Tech Hub help
sections.summary: By the third quarter of 2017, businesses can get in-person help at IMDA's SME Digital Tech Hub.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: By the third quarter of 2017, businesses will be able to get in-person help at the SME Digital Tech Hub set up by IMDA.

sections.label: Planned Cybersecurity Bill
sections.summary: MCI plans to table a Cybersecurity Bill later this year covering Critical Information Infrastructure and CSA powers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Members may be aware that the Ministry of Communications and Information (MCI) is planning to table a Cybersecurity Bill later this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: The Cybersecurity Bill will ensure that owners and operators of Critical Information Infrastructure take proactive steps to secure their systems and networks and report incidents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: It will also empower CSA to respond to cyber threats, facilitate the sharing of cybersecurity information and raise the standards of cybersecurity providers in Singapore.

sections.label: Widened CMCA jurisdiction
sections.summary: Widening CMCA jurisdiction lets Police investigate overseas acts causing serious harm or risk in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: The widening of the jurisdiction of CMCA will enable the Police to investigate cases where the criminal act resulted in serious harm or created a significant risk of serious harm in Singapore, even if the perpetrator was overseas at the material time and targeted a computer overseas.

sections.label: CMCA offences as extraditable
sections.summary: MHA is working with MinLaw to specify CMCA offences as extradition offences.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: MHA is working with the Ministry of Law (MinLaw) to specify offences under CMCA as extradition offences.

sections.label: Public-private cybercrime platform
sections.summary: Police established a public-private industry platform with software companies, telcos and banks on cybercrime detection and prevention.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: With greater awareness, the private sector is better able to help the Police to detect cybercrimes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: This year, Police established a public-private industry platform to foster closer collaboration with software companies, telcos and banks on cybercrime detection and prevention.

sections.label: Police scam enforcement operations
sections.summary: Last year the Police ran five island-wide scam enforcement operations, arresting over 300 people involving about $1.8 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Last year, the Police conducted five island-wide enforcement operations targeting scams.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: More than 300 people were arrested in connection with scam cases, involving about $1.8 million in total.

sections.label: E-commerce cheating reports decrease
sections.summary: E-commerce cheating reports, about half of online scam cases, fell 6% last year from 2,239 cases in 2015 to 2,105 in 2016.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Notably, the number of reports of cheating cases involving e-commerce, which forms about half of all online scam cases, decreased by 6% last year, from 2,239 cases in 2015 to 2,105 cases in 2016.
